testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Welded wheel rims should:

options.text: Be placed in the front of the vehicle.
Be placed in the rear of the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Welded wheels and rims are not safe. Replace any damaged wheels and rims.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Drive straight into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: You should check and adjust your mirrors:
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors before you start driving. Your posture changes daily, so your mirrors may need adjustment.

questions.question: A Class 1 hazardous material is:
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are explosives. Examples include ammunition, dynamite, and fireworks.

questions.question: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal unnecessarily can:

options.text: Release air faster than it can be replaced.
Add more air to a brake system.
Make the brake pedal harder to depress.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air faster than it can be replaced.
questions.explanation: In vehicles with air brakes, pressing and releasing the brake pedal too often lets air out faster than the compressor can replace it. This causes air pressure to drop and the brakes may stop working.

questions.question: Engine belts should:
questions.explanation: When checking your engine, look at the belts for tightness and wear. The right amount of give varies by vehicle, so learn what is correct for your vehicle.

questions.question: Pre-trip inspections:

options.text: Should never be done the same way two times in a row.
Should always be done in the same order.
Do not need to be done if the driver is familiar with the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should always be done in the same order.
questions.explanation: Do your vehicle inspection in the same order every time. This helps you remember all the steps and makes sure you don't miss anything.

questions.question: At speeds below 40 mph, maintain at least ____ of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle length.
questions.explanation: Below 40 mph, allow one second of following distance for every 10 feet of vehicle length. At faster speeds, use the same formula and add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning signal comes on in a vehicle with air brakes, the driver should:

options.text: Test the brakes while driving, but continue if nothing seems wrong.
Drive with the hazard lights activated.

questions.explanation: When the low air pressure warning comes on, stop and park the vehicle safely as soon as possible. You must stop while you still have some braking power left.

questions.question: Distracted driving:

options.text: Only happens when people physically do something while driving.
Can happen from mental activities, such as daydreaming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen from mental activities, such as daydreaming.
questions.explanation: Distractions can be physical (reaching for an object), mental (talking with a passenger), or both (holding a phone). Avoid distraction by pre-programming radio stations, planning your route ahead, avoiding difficult conversations while driving, adjusting mirrors before leaving, and not eating, drinking, or smoking while driving.

questions.question: How does a vehicle's center of gravity height affect driving?

options.text: It has no effect on how the vehicle handles.
It greatly affects how safely you can handle the vehicle.
It should not matter when loading cargo.
It only matters if your route has many hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: It greatly affects how safely you can handle the vehicle.
questions.explanation: A vehicle's center of gravity height is very important for safe handling. Always load cargo as low as possible in the vehicle.

questions.question: What two things tell you when to shift to a higher gear?
questions.explanation: Two indicators tell you when to shift up. First is engine speed (rpm) — check your manual for the correct rpm range. Second is road speed (mph) — learn which speeds work for each gear and watch your speedometer.

questions.question: How should you brake when using ABS?
questions.explanation: When using an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), brake the same way you would in any vehicle. Do not change your braking technique.

questions.question: What must you do when exiting a bus?
questions.explanation: When exiting a bus during the vehicle control test, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. Always keep holding the handrail. Not exiting correctly may cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: What is blocking used for?

options.text: To put cargo in a large box.
To stop cargo from sliding in a trailer.
To stop cargo from falling out of a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: To stop cargo from sliding in a trailer.
questions.explanation: Blocking is placed around cargo to keep it from sliding while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: What causes distracted driving?
questions.explanation: Driving distractions can be physical (like reaching for an object), mental (like talking with a passenger), or both (like holding a phone to text).

questions.question: Which person should NOT concern a driver?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger in their car.
A child on the side of the road.
A construction worker on the side of the road.
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus.
questions.explanation: Be careful around people who are not paying attention to the road. Watch out for drivers talking to passengers, children near the road, and road workers.

questions.question: What is the maximum leakage rate for a double combination vehicle during an air leakage test?
questions.explanation: Know the safe air loss rate for your vehicle. A double combination vehicle should not lose more than 4 psi per minute during an air leakage test.

questions.question: What should you use when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: It is best to avoid driving in fog. If you must drive in fog, use your low beam headlights. Do not use high beams — they reflect off the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What are escape ramps?

options.text: Ramps to quickly exit the interstate.
Ramps that connect four-lane and two-lane highways.
Ramps that stop runaway vehicles on steep hills.
Ramps that cannot be used by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ramps that stop runaway vehicles on steep hills.
questions.explanation: Escape ramps are built on steep downhill sections to safely stop runaway vehicles. They have a long bed of loose, soft material and sometimes an uphill slope.

questions.question: When you start a truck with a trailer, how do you know the ABS is not working?

options.text: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
The red light on the right side of the trailer flashes three times.
All the rear lights flash and then turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
questions.explanation: When you start the engine, dashboard lights should turn on and then turn off. If the ABS warning light stays on, the system is not working. On a truck with a trailer, if the yellow light on the left rear stays on after starting, the ABS is not working properly.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to affect your body?

options.text: After several drinks have been consumed.

questions.explanation: Alcohol affects muscle control, reaction time, vision, and judgment. For some people, one drink is enough to cause impairment. The safest choice is to never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Which one is not a reason to use your mirrors?

options.text: You are looking at fuel prices.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are looking at fuel prices.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. This is especially important when turning, changing lanes, merging, or making tight maneuvers.

questions.question: If you drive a truck that needs a CDL:

options.text: You do not need to wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only if you are carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo.
You must always wear a seat belt.
You must wear a seat belt only when driving a tank trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt.
questions.explanation: For safety, you must wear your seat belt at all times when operating a commercial vehicle.

questions.question: What does the application pressure gauge show?

options.text: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
The temperature of air in the braking system.
The pressure of air coming from the compressor.
How many times the brakes have been used.

questions.correctAnswerText: How much air pressure is being applied to the brakes.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, the application pressure gauge shows how much air pressure is being applied to the brakes. Not all vehicles with air brakes have this gauge.

questions.question: If your driver's license is suspended, what must you do?

options.text: You do not have to tell anyone.
It will not affect your CDL.

questions.explanation: You must tell your employer within 30 days of any traffic conviction. If your license is suspended, revoked, or canceled, you must tell your employer within two business days.

questions.question: A 40-foot-long item on a flatbed trailer needs at least ____ tie-down(s).
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo length. Always use at least two tie-downs, no matter the size.

questions.question: After starting the engine, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn off once the vehicle starts moving.

questions.explanation: After the engine starts, all warning lights and buzzers should turn off immediately. The charging circuit, oil, coolant, and ABS lights should all turn off.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, what should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.

questions.explanation: Get out of the aggressive driver's way. Do not make eye contact or gesture at them. Report them to the police when you can do so safely.

questions.question: Hydroplaning usually happens:

options.text: In areas where water collects on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: In areas where water collects on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs where water builds up on the road. It can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water. Hydroplaning is more likely with under-inflated or worn tires.

questions.question: What is a retarder?

options.text: A device that slows down a vehicle
A device that reduces engine noise

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that slows down a vehicle
questions.explanation: Retarders help slow vehicles. This reduces how much drivers need to use the brakes.

questions.question: During the skills test, if you need to stop before making a turn, you should:

options.text: Stop after the stop line for a better view

questions.explanation: Stop smoothly behind any stop line or stop sign. Keep your front wheels straight ahead. Do not let your vehicle roll. Stop where you can still see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.question: What does an Individual Vehicle Distance Record (IVDR) NOT need to include?
questions.explanation: An IVDR must include the distance traveled and fuel purchased. It must show trip dates and total distance. It does not need to show how many vehicles were passed.

questions.question: A thin layer of ice on a road surface is called:
questions.explanation: Black ice is a clear, thin layer of ice. You can see the road through it. It may look like wet pavement. Be careful when temperatures drop below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: During a trip, gauges are:

options.text: The only way to spot vehicle problems
One way to spot vehicle problems

questions.correctAnswerText: One way to spot vehicle problems
questions.explanation: Check gauges and instrument panels often during a trip. Also check mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights for problems.

questions.question: Mirrors should be used:

options.text: By a helper to check blind spots

questions.explanation: Check the mirrors on both sides of your vehicle frequently while driving.

questions.question: Which sign shows standing water on the road?
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning can happen where water pools on the road. Clear reflections, tire splashes, and raindrops on the pavement all show standing water.

questions.question: When going downhill, a vehicle will:

options.text: Travel at the same speed as on flat road

questions.explanation: Gravity causes vehicles to speed up on downgrades. Slow down before reaching a hill to avoid overusing brakes.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use ____ air brake systems.
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: Alcohol leaves the body:
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Coffee and cold showers do not speed this up. The only way to become sober is to give your body time to remove the alcohol.

questions.question: When carrying a wide load, a driver should:

options.text: Get special permits and follow special rules, like driving only at certain times.
Honk at other drivers to make them move out of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits and follow special rules, like driving only at certain times.
questions.explanation: Wide, long, or heavy loads need special permits. These loads may only be allowed on the road at certain times of the day.

questions.question: Service brakes should:

options.text: Only be tested by a trained mechanic.

questions.explanation: Always check your service brakes before you drive. Testing them before each trip helps you find problems before you need to brake on the road.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a warning sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Warning signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, blinking frequently, and heavy eyelids. Other signs are yawning often, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, not remembering the last few miles, missing exits or signs, trouble keeping your head up, drifting from your lane, following too closely, hitting rumble strips, and feeling restless or irritable.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use:
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. These have two separate braking systems controlled by one set of controls. Each system operates the brakes on different axles.

questions.question: When traveling long distances, you should:
questions.explanation: On a long trip, take a break after every 100 miles or two hours of driving to avoid fatigue. Driving through the night or during times when you would normally sleep increases the risk of fatigue.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Allow rain water to enter the tanks.
Remove water and oil from the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the tanks.
questions.explanation: Air brake system tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil. If left in the system, water and oil can damage the brakes.

questions.question: When driving down a steep grade:

options.text: You should use your brakes all the way down.
Shift into a higher gear to slow down.
Shift into lower gears to slow down.
Put the truck in neutral to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into lower gears to slow down.
questions.explanation: On a steep grade, use the engine's braking power to slow down. Use your brakes only to help slow the vehicle and prevent overheating.

questions.question: If you have more than one license:

options.text: You are unlikely to be caught.
There is no way for authorities to find out.

questions.explanation: You cannot have more than one license. Breaking this law can result in jail time and/or a fine of up to $5,000.

questions.question: When using road speed to decide when to shift gears, you should:

options.text: Learn what speeds work for each gear and shift up when needed.
Watch other vehicles and try to match their speed.
Watch other trucks and shift when they shift.
Use the speed limit as a guide.

questions.correctAnswerText: Learn what speeds work for each gear and shift up when needed.
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift to a higher gear. First is engine speed (rpm). Read your vehicle's manual to learn the correct rpm range and shift up when you reach the top. Second is road speed (mph). Learn which speeds work for each gear, watch your speedometer, and shift up as needed.

questions.question: If you are unsure if your vehicle can safely pass under a bridge, you should:

options.text: Swerve as you pass under the bridge.

questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under an overhead object, slow down and find another route if possible.
